## Appearance

Priscilla Grant is a fair and pale young woman with a spiritual appearance. She has been seen dressed in golden silk attire.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v2 XX The Way It Often Happens P22](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0022)_

## Personality

A student at the [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy), Priscilla Grant is known for her thoughtful, imaginative, and ambitious nature. Despite her pale, spiritual appearance, she is also full of mischief, pranks, and fun.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)_

## History

Priscilla Grant attended Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) alongside [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), and she later worked as a teacher at [Carmody](../codex/places.md#carmody) school. During a spring birthday outing, she explored the woods and [Hester](../character/hester-gray.md) Gray's forgotten garden with [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Diana](../character/diana.md), and Jane. She eventually wrote to [Anne](../character/anne.md) to explain why famous author Mrs. [Morgan](../character/morgan.md) had missed a planned dinner party, but she later accompanied Mrs. [Morgan](../character/morgan.md) to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) herself, arriving while [Anne](../character/anne.md) was dealing with a dyed nose. When [Anne](../character/anne.md) moved to [Kingsport](../codex/places.md#kingsport) to begin her studies at [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), Priscilla met her at the train station and brought her to their initial boardinghouse. Soon after, while visiting a cemetery, Priscilla and [Anne](../character/anne.md) befriended [Philippa Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md), quickly expanding their social circle at college. Looking to improve their living situation for their second year, Priscilla joined [Anne](../character/anne.md) in arranging to rent a house called Patty's Place alongside [Stella Maynard](../character/stella-maynard.md) and Philippa. She continued to share in the domestic and social life at Patty's Place throughout her remaining time at [Redmond](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), visiting [Anne](../character/anne.md) in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) over the summer and ultimately completing her studies to graduate alongside her friends on [Convocation](../codex/places.md#convocation) day.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P46](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0046), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P47](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0047), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Quotes

> "I’m so sorry, but I’m afraid we won’t get up to Green Gables at all now, for by the time Aunty’s ankle is well she will have to go back to Toronto. She has to be there by a certain date."
>
> — Priscilla Grant — [v2 XVII A Chapter of Accidents P63](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0063)

> “And oh, Anne dear,” wrote Priscilla, “I’m so sorry, but I’m afraid we won’t get up to Green Gables at all now, for by the time Aunty’s ankle is well she will have to go back to Toronto. She has to be there by a certain date.”
>
> — Priscilla Grant — [v2 XVII A Chapter of Accidents P63](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0063)

> "She talks as much about boys as Ruby Gillis does. But it always enrages or sickens me to hear Ruby, whereas I just wanted to laugh good-naturedly at Phil. Now, what is the why of that?"
>
> — Priscilla Grant — [v3 ch.Lady P70](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0070)

> "It would be too good to be true. Fairy tales don’t happen nowadays. I won’t hope, Anne. The disappointment would be too awful to bear. They’re sure to want more for it than we can afford. Remember, it’s on Spofford Avenue."
>
> — Priscilla Grant — [v3 ch.Friend P31](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0031)

> "This cake is now what you might call a flat failure. And the cushion is likewise ruined. Never tell me that Friday isn’t unlucky."
>
> — Priscilla Grant — [v3 ch.Gardners’Call P35](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0035)
